DISCUSSION ITEMS a.
Review of the Enacted Budget Vice President Abby Benson noted that the official State budget has not been approved yet.
She provided a brief overview of the University’s FY25 Budget request, specifically the requests for an operating budget increase, Rhode Island Capital Plan Fund (RICAP), and a Biomedical Sciences Building General Obligation (GO) Bond.
With respect to the operating budget increases, she noted that URI requested a $32.1M increase, the legislature recommended a $5.4M increase.
With respect to RICAP asset protection funding, she noted that URI requested $16.3M, the legislature recommended $14.0M.
With respect to the Biomedical Sciences GO Bond, she noted that URI requested $87.45M, the legislature recommended $87.5M.
She provided additional detail regarding the operating budget increase request and the RICAP request (specifically related to PFAS remediation efforts).

Responding to questions, Vice President Benson noted that budget shortfalls are traditionally managed though the use of reserves to meet contractual obligations and also that the pending new budget model will allow the University to clearly evaluate and reset the University’s budget.
She also noted that the appropriation from the state is roughly 20% of the University’s education and general budget. b.
Report of Actions Taken in Executive Session Briar Lane Acquisition Enclosure Vice President Benson reported the action taken in Executive Session by the Board of Trustees Finance and Facilities Committee on April 4, 2024, and by the Board of Trustees on April 26, 2024, to approve the acquisition of property at 63 Briar Lane, Kingston, RI.
She noted that, following the Board’s approval in April, the University is currently completing the purchase of this property. 3.

DISCUSSION ITEMS a.
Projected FY24 Performance vs.
Budget; and IBB Update Enclosure 2.a.
Chair Ownjazayeri introduced Abby Benson, Vice President for Administration and Finance, who provided the annual report on FY24 financial performance.
The presentation can be found in Enclosure 2a.
She discussed the FY24 forecast, with least likely and most likely scenarios compared to budget.
She expects that, despite the budgeted deficit of $4.1M, the University will end the year positively, between $6.6M and $14.8M in surplus.
She noted that some of these increases are one-time only.
Vice President Benson also provided a brief update on the Incentive Based Budget (IBB) model, providing a broad overview of the model as well as the current schedule for the model’s implementation.

Vice President Benson answered questions from Committee members on how the University is using information from other institutions regarding their challenges and successes implementing IBB (or similar models) and the broad differences between incremental and IBB budget models.
President Marc Parlange briefly discussed the entrepreneurial nature of incentive-based budgets and the need for this model for the University, given the limits of the incremental model.
Vice President Benson noted that the University is currently developing materials that will describe the flow of funds and the specific drivers for budget determination. b.
Initial Review of the FY2026 – FY2030 Capital Improvement Plan Enclosure 2.b.
Vice President Benson provided a presentation on the University’s Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) for FY2026—FY2030.
The presentation can be found in Enclosure 2.b.
Vice President Benson noted that the current presentation differs somewhat from previous presentations, with an extensive slide deck provided to the Committee, but a detailed discussion only on changes to the current plan and priority items.

She discussed the overall development of the CIP, including levels of approval and the process for adding new projects to the CIP.
She provided a high-level view of the CIP, noting completed, updated, and new projects.
The Committee discussed the impact of project cost escalation overall.
Committee members suggested that the University provide broad context on escalation when discussing URI project costs with the state.
Vice President Benson alerted the Committee to the receipt of four responses to the Request for Qualifications regarding the public-private-partnership (P3) for new University housing.
She discussed the General Obligation Bond strategy relative to the current CIP submission, noting that the pending Campus Master Planning effort will help inform the 2026 and 2028 bond referendums.
She also discussed the current Kushner (bond) authorizations, with details on their status.

Update on Classification and Compensation Study Enclosure 2.f.
Vice President Benson provided an update on the University’s (Human Resources/HR) Classification and Compensation Study, noting that the University has been working to implement this study for several years and presently has a consultant engaged.
The study only concerns non-classified, non- faculty employees.

The goal of this study is to modernize the University’s HR function and provide an updated job classification architecture, with new position descriptions, a new pay plan structure, a market study and equity analysis, a preliminary Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) review, and an implementation roadmap.
She also provided a high-level overview of the project phases.

TO: The University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees, Finance and Facilities Committee FROM: Marc B.
Parlange, Ph.D., P.Eng., President DATE: June 26, 2025 SUBJECT: Action Item: Approval of the FY2027―FY2031 Capital Improvement Plan Purpose of Submittal: To purpose of this action is to seek Board of Trustees approval for the submission of the University of Rhode Island FY2027―FY2031 Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) to the State of Rhode Island.
Points to Consider: Every year it is the responsibility of the University to submit a CIP to the State of Rhode Island.
The CIP identifies and lists in order of priority capital projects (both proposed or in progress) of $1 million or more funded with unrestricted funds.
This submission is a critical and required step to secure funding to support the physical assets at the University advancing both educational and research programs.

The enclosed presentation provides updat es to existing CIP projects scope/budget/schedule, including the Narragansett Bay Campus Phase 1 and 2 projects, the Fine Arts Center, the Athletics Complex Renewal, the Biomedical Sciences Building, and New Undergraduate Housing.
It also provides information for the Memorial Union and Health and Counseling Center projects, which have been on hold for the last several years to prioritize housing.
The presentation also highlights several additions made to the CIP last year, with a heavy emphasis on addressing the significant backlog of asset renewal needed on URI’s buildings, which in total comprise 28% of the State’s buildings.
These additions incl ude improving campus accessibility, access control, building envelope integrity, and refurbishment of the Carothers Library HVAC systems and the university’s water tower.

Two new projects are proposed to be added to the CIP this year, replacement of the Allen Harbor Bulkhead and Dock, which is necessary to protect the site and maintain access to our small boats that provide both educational and research support, and a project currently underway to renovate Washburn Hall and the Carlotti Building to provide space needed to empty Tucker House and Adams House in anticipation of future mixed-use development on Upper College Road.
The CIP also recommends a 2026 General Obligation (GO) Bond project for an Integrated Health Building.
The Integrated Health Buildin g would provide expanded programming to support interprofessional education and clinical training in the health disciplines.
URI is currently contemplating the construction of a new Student Success building on the current site of the Carlotti Building on the quad for the 2028 GO Bond.

Slides 8, 9, and 11 of the enclosed presentation highlight in blue changes from the Draft CIP reviewed by the committee in April, as follows: • We are repeating our full ask for Campus Accessibility and Building Envelope impr ovements, both of which will likely be funded in part by the legislature this year. • The former Blue Technology Innovation Center is now named the Ocean Technology Innovation Center, which was recently awarded funding by the Department of Commerce. • The project costs for Narragansett Bay Campus Phase 2 have been increased slightly to include additional donations to support equipment, and the project cost for repairing the bulkhead at Allen Harbor has been increased after an initial design effort. Recommendation: I recommend that the Board of Trustees approve the enclosed University of Rhode Island Capital Improvement Plan for FY2027-FY2031. Supporting Information: Please see University of Rhode Island FY2027-FY2031 Capital Improvement Plan Enclosure Proposed Motion of the Board: THAT, the Board of Trustees approve the University of Rhode Island Capital Improvement Plan for FY2027-FY2031 as presented.
CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PLAN FY27-FY31 Presentation to Board of Trustees – Finance and Facilities June 26, 2025

What is the Capital Improvement Plan? • 5 Year plan that shows projects that have a total project cost of greater than $1 Million • It is a rolling plan that is submitted annually as a request to the state, typically in July. Who Approves the Capital Improvement Plan? • There are 5 levels of approval. They are: • University of Rhode Island - Facilities Committee (internal) (March & May) • University of Rhode Island - President’s Executive Council (March & May) • University of Rhode Island - Board of Trustees (April & June) • Executive Branch • Analysis performed and Recommendations made by the Office of Management and Budget (July-December) • Final Recommended Capital Budget by the Governor’s Office (Third week of January) • Legislative Branch • Analysis performed and Recommendations made by both the House and Senate Fiscal Offices (January – June) • Final Plan approved as part of the RI Budget Appropriations Bill (June) How is a project added to the Capital Improvement Plan? • In order to receive consideration, all projects must be submitted on the Capital Improvement Request form by a member of the Senior Leadership to the URI Office of Planning & Real Estate Development • Most projects will have an advanced planning study performed prior to inclusion in the Capital Improvement plan to determine program, siting, massing, and total expected project cost
What does the Capital Improvement Plan cover? The University of Rhode Island’s Board of Trustees is responsible for about 28% of the State’s total real estate portfolio.

Campus Access Control Project Statistics: • Current evaluation of a university-wide Access Control systems is underway. In order to provide a safer campus environment, there will be a need to update the software and hardware systems to allow for a secure campus and quick responses to emergencies such as lockdown for an active shooter event. This project will provide the core infrastructure that will allow subsequent projects to connect buildings to this centralized system. • $ 1,575,000 - RICAP • Funding for subsequent building upgrades and connection to this centralized system will be needed. Level of future support needed TBD. • Status: Pending Funding Approval • Start 2026 • Complete 2027 FY27 Request Access Control Systems

New Water Tower Project Statistics: • Built in 1971, the current water tower requires refurbishment, which will be supported by one of the Utility RIHEBC bonds. In addition, additional water capacity is needed to support the expanding campus footprint and fire compliance needs. Recommend building new tower after refurbishing existing tower. • $ 10,700,000 - RICAP • Status: Pending Funding Approval • Start 2027 • Complete 2030 Kingston Campus - Locus Map FY28 Request Existing URI Water Tower

Project Statistics: • The Ocean Technology Innovation Center (OTIC) will be managed by the University of Rhode Island Research Foundation. The OTIC will accommodate a mix of incubator/innovation and start-up spaces that will be rented to commercial entities, leveraging URI’s marine research community, ocean engineering assets and access to Narragansett Bay to contribute to the development of the state’s blue technology sector. • $5,700,000 - Third-Party (Innovation Campus) • Status: Pending Funding Approval • Start 2026 • Complete 2029 Narraganset Bay Campus - Locus Map Ocean Technology Innovation Center Ongoing Project POTENTIAL OTIC
